eggs.intro: Eggs are items you pick up, not Pokémon you find. What you can hatch depends on the distance on the Egg, and each distance comes from somewhere different.

rarity.detail: In game, tapping an Egg lists what can hatch from it, ordered by rarity from one Egg icon (most common) to five (most rare). In general the further an Egg makes you walk, the rarer what comes out.

sources.detail: Spinning a PokéStop can give you an Egg along with the usual items. This is where ordinary 2 km, 5 km and 10 km Eggs come from.
sources.label: PokéStops and Gyms

sources.detail: Opening a Gift can give you an Egg as well as items and Stardust. Rows tagged Gift exchange are the ones that hatch from these.
sources.label: Gifts from friends

sources.detail: Beating Sierra, Cliff or Arlo gives a Strange Egg, which needs 12 km to hatch. You need free space in your Egg inventory, Pokémon storage and Item Bag before the battle or you will not get one.
sources.label: Team GO Rocket Leaders — 12 km Strange Eggs

sources.detail: Rows tagged Adventure Sync hatch from the bonus Eggs awarded for hitting a weekly walking distance, not from Eggs you pick up at a PokéStop. Adventure Sync itself is the setting that counts your steps while the app is closed — turning it on does not by itself give you these Eggs; walking the weekly distance does.
sources.label: Adventure Sync weekly rewards

entries.detail: Most often the reward for a seven-day Field Research breakthrough, and from GO Battle League end-of-set rewards. Not a PokéStop drop.

items.intro: Some evolutions need an item as well as Candy. Which Pokémon need which item is read straight from the game data; how you get the item is not in that data, so those lines are hand-researched and labelled.

acquisitionGuide.note: Where Eggs and special Evolution items actually come from. The egg feed tags rows 'Adventure Sync' and 'Gift exchange' and explains neither, and the origin lines on ranked cards say 'needs Sinnoh Stone' without saying how to get one. Claims are split by how well they are sourced: `sourced` entries cite a frozen official Niantic page in sourceRefs; `handResearched` entries do NOT, and the app labels them as such rather than presenting them at the same confidence.
